items.title: Kenny Davern interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 16, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: he was with Bob Haggart or Miff Mole, and the people who matter — George Wettling, you know, guys who played the kind of music I liked at that time

ctx.x: And you’d been playing clarinet for a few years.

About four years, three or four years. I don’t remember how serious it was, but I remember playing, you know with the piano playing the “Twelve Street Rag” at an assembly period. “Now we’ll see ‘The Heavens are Telling’ by Ludwig von Beethoven to be followed by John Kenneth Davern performing on the clarinet “The Twelfth Street Rag.” And I remember how awful it was trying to finger the Albert System playing because [scats] I got messed up. items.title: Bob Haggart interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, September 22, 1995
items.q: We just pick out some songs and whatever Kenny wants to play we play. Right? Kenny picks the tunes usually, and Warren goes along with anything.

ctx.x: And you made arrangements also for the smaller group that played out of that?

Well, we didn’t have arrangements for the Bob Cats, that was strictly head arrangements, faked you know. Figure out a little introduction or something sometimes, and we’d just talk over it the first time we’d run it down, we’d say you do this and I’ll take sixteen, then Eddie will play eight, then we’ll play stops, then we’ll play drum breaks, and you know, you’d talk it over. You don’t have any music. Well that’s the way we are this thing we’re doing this weekend. We don’t have music. We just pick out some songs…

If you were explaining to students that you knew were going to see this tape, could you explain to them how much vocabulary a jazz musician has to bring to the table in order to do that, in order to have guys, maybe he’s never played with just call tunes and be able to make it through those tunes.

items.title: Kenny Davern interviewed by Michael Woods, Clinton, New York, September 23, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: most recently in a string ensemble format with arrangements by Bob Haggart.

ctx.x: Kenny Davern is the leading jazz clarinetist of our day. Born in 1935, a native of Huntington, NY, his recording debut came at the age of 19 with Jack Teagarden. Career highlights include work with Buck Clayton, Red Allen and the Dukes of Dixieland. His soprano sax work was featured with Bob Wilber and Soprano Summit. Since 1979 he has toured with various quartets and recorded frequently, most recently in a string ensemble format with arrangements by Bob Haggart. Davern is a player of outstanding technical skills…
